types.name: FArcUIViewInfo
types.doc:
What SyncWorldWidgets needs from the host's camera to place world-anchored
widget trees on the screen-space overlay: the combined view-projection, the
viewport it maps into and where the camera is (for distance scale/fade).

members.name: CameraUp
members.doc:
Camera world up, for the true-3D billboard path (SyncWorldWidgets3D).
The screen-space SyncWorldWidgets path ignores it.

types.name: FArcUIWorldQuad
types.doc:
One resolved world-space UI widget quad for the host to draw as a real
in-scene quad through SceneRenderer::SubmitWorldWidgetQuad. WorldMatrix maps a
unit quad (centered on the origin, XY plane) to world space — already a
camera-facing billboard or a transform-oriented plane. Texture is the
offscreen-rendered widget tree, owned by the screen stack's world-widget
renderer and valid for the frame; the host wraps it in a Ref to submit.

types.name: EArcUIInputDevice
types.doc:
Last-used input device — switches the visible gamepad focus highlight on
and off the way CommonUI does.

types.name: FArcUIWorldHit
types.doc: The result of a ray hit against the interactive world-widget quads.

types.name: CArcUIScreenStack
types.doc:
Runtime owner of the live game-UI overlays. Scans a World for
ArcUIComponents, hosts code-driven Push/Pop screens next to them,
instantiates each visible one from its .ui asset, composites them
(ZOrder-sorted) into a single overlay the host mounts into its Arc root,
re-resolves data bindings every Tick, routes widget events to the host's
event sink and drives directional (gamepad/keyboard) focus navigation.

members.name: SetPathResolver
members.doc:
Resolves a serialized asset path ("Content/UI/x.ui") to something
LoadFromFile can open. Identity when unset.

members.name: SetFocusSink
members.doc:
Where directional nav sends the newly focused widget (host wires this to
its Arc input processor's SetFocus). Optional.

members.name: SetBindingResolver
members.doc:
Supplies the current value for a widget data-binding source. Applied to
bound widgets at instantiation, then re-resolved every Tick with a
dirty-check so bound widgets track live gameplay state. Optional —
without it authored defaults stand. Set it before the first SyncFromWorld.

members.name: SetEventSink
members.doc:
Receives (widgetName, eventName, action) for every authored widget event
that fires. Optional; without it events are dropped.

members.name: InstallVfsPathResolver
members.doc:
Convenience installers so every host mounts identically. The VFS path
resolver maps "Content/UI/x.ui" to a native path; the bridge focus
sink drives CArcMowoBridge's input processor; the world binding resolver
wires FArcUIBindingLibrary reflection paths against the host's live
World + entity-name lookup (customHook is the Visual Script seam).

members.name: InstallWorldBindingResolver
members.signature: void InstallWorldBindingResolver(FArcUIBindingLibrary::FWorldProvider world, FArcUIBindingLibrary::FEntityLookup lookup, FArcUIBindingLibrary::FCustomSourceHook customHook = FArcUIBindingLibrary::FCustomSourceHook())

members.name: EnableHotReload
members.doc:
Watches every loaded .ui file and rebuilds its screens on save.
Watch callbacks only record intent; the rebuild happens in Tick.

members.name: LoadLocalization
members.signature: static uint32_t LoadLocalization(const std::string& rootDir, const std::string& locale)
members.doc:
Loads <rootDir>/<locale>/*.txt string tables (key=value lines, file stem
= namespace) into Arc's CTextLocalizationManager and makes the locale
current, so authored text_key props resolve through CText::FromKey.
Returns the number of entries registered.

members.name: SetProjectTheme
members.doc:
Theme every screen without its own `theme:` resolves colour tokens
against. Loaded through the path resolver and cached; empty clears back
to the built-in default theme.

members.name: SetSafeZoneInsets
members.doc:
Title-safe insets as a fraction of each axis, applied by every screen's
root canvas (the designer's Safe Area overlay draws the same box).

members.name: SyncWorldWidgets
members.signature: void SyncWorldWidgets(World& world, const FArcUIViewInfo& view)
members.doc:
Places every visible ArcUIWorldWidgetComponent's tree at its entity's
projected screen position. Call once per frame after the camera is
resolved; an invalid view hides the layer instead of dropping the trees.
This is the screen-space fallback — components with worldSpace = false use
it exclusively, and everything falls back to it when the offscreen
renderer is unavailable.

members.name: FWorldQuadSink
members.doc:
The true-3D path: for every visible worldSpace ArcUIWorldWidgetComponent,
(re-)renders its tree into an offscreen texture at a distance-driven LOD
resolution — only when the widget is dirty or its LOD bucket moved, so an
idle nameplate never re-renders — computes its billboard/oriented world
quad, and hands each quad to `sink` for the host to submit to the scene
renderer. Widgets with worldSpace = false are skipped here (drive them
through SyncWorldWidgets instead). No-ops without a world-widget renderer.

members.name: SyncWorldWidgets3D
members.signature: void SyncWorldWidgets3D(World& world, const FArcUIViewInfo& view, const FWorldQuadSink& sink)

members.name: MarkWorldWidgetDirty
members.doc:
Marks a world widget's offscreen texture stale so the next
SyncWorldWidgets3D re-renders it. Bound widgets whose data changed call
this automatically; hosts can force a refresh (e.g. a health bar tick).

members.name: HitTestWorldWidgets
members.signature: FArcUIWorldHit HitTestWorldWidgets(const Vec3& rayOrigin, const Vec3& rayDir) const
members.doc:
Ray-vs-quad hit test against the interactive world-widget quads resolved
by the last SyncWorldWidgets3D, nearest hit first. On a hit, the local UV
is filled in (top-left origin, matching the widget's own coordinates).

members.name: RouteWorldWidgetClick
members.signature: bool RouteWorldWidgetClick(const Vec3& rayOrigin, const Vec3& rayDir)
members.doc:
Ray-picks the nearest interactive world widget and dispatches a synthetic
left click (button down + up) to the widget under the mapped local point,
exactly as if the user had clicked that pixel of the offscreen tree.
Returns true when a widget consumed it.

members.name: PushScreen
members.signature: int32_t PushScreen(const std::string& assetPath, int32_t zOrder = 1000, bool modal = false)
members.doc:
Code-driven screens (pause menu, main menu, loading). Returns a handle
for PopScreen; 0 on load failure. Modal screens contain gamepad focus
and report through HasModalScreen so the host can gate game input.

members.name: PlayAnimation
members.signature: bool PlayAnimation(const std::string& assetPath, const std::string& name)
members.doc:
Timeline playback on a mounted screen (world-scanned or pushed),
addressed by its asset path. The two-argument form starts with the
authored loop flag; the params form overrides loop/reverse and takes a
completion callback (fired once, after the end pose is applied; looping
runs never finish). Playing an already-running animation restarts it.
Every finished run also reports through the event sink as
(assetPath, "anim_finished", animationName).

The built-in event-action vocabulary: "PlayAnim:Name",

through this before reaching the host's event sink; hosts and tests can
dispatch the same verbs directly. Returns true when the action was one
of the built-ins (whether or not the animation existed).

members.signature: Arcf::AVideoPlayer* FindVideoPlayer(const std::string& assetPath, const std::string& widgetName) const
members.doc:
The VideoPlayer node under a name (empty screen path searches every
screen), or null when the name is not a video — MUIStatics' seam.

members.signature: void SetVisualScriptBindingText(const std::string& name, const std::string& text)

members.name: SetVisualScriptBindingNumber
members.signature: void SetVisualScriptBindingNumber(const std::string& name, double number)

members.name: NotifyAssetChanged
members.doc:
Marks a loaded asset stale so the next Tick evicts and rebuilds every
screen using it — the entry point the file watcher drives, public so
hosts without a watcher (and tests) can force the same reload.

members.name: HandleDirectional
members.doc:
Directional navigation: spatial pick of the nearest focusable widget
in the pressed direction (center-line projection with axis bias, the
UE approach). Falls back to the linear cycle only when the tree has no
usable geometry (headless). Focusability comes from the AWidget
IsFocusable predicate, not a type whitelist. The focused widget's
navigation rules (nav_up / nav_down / nav_left / nav_right on its node or
an ancestor) can stop the move, wrap it at the edge, or send it to a
named widget instead.

members.name: SetRightToLeft
members.doc:
The reading order screens build with when a node says "inherit" — set
from the active culture. Takes effect on the next (re)build; call
before pushing, or push again after switching.

members.name: HandleAccept
members.doc:
Accept delivered as a real activate on the focused widget (the widget
translates it internally — click delegate, toggle, open); no
synthesized mouse events.

members.name: HandleBack
members.doc:
Back/cancel: a host- or screen-defined handler first, then pop of the
top code-driven screen.

members.name: NotifyInputDevice
members.doc:
Hosts report the device each input event came from; switching to the
gamepad re-applies the focus visual, switching to the mouse clears it.

types.name: CArcUIWorldWidgetRenderer
types.doc:
Renders an Arc widget tree into an offscreen engine texture so the scene
renderer can draw it as a real in-world quad (nameplates, ping markers). It
reuses Arc's own CArcUIRenderer against the bridge-adopted device — it is not
a second UI renderer, just a second target — and records into the engine's
current command buffer through the RHI facade, one small render pass per
widget. Each widget keeps its own resolution-sized target and is only
re-rendered when the screen stack marks it dirty (content changed or the
distance LOD bucket moved), so an idle nameplate costs nothing per frame.

The offscreen pass runs under the engine's negative-height (Vulkan Y-flip)
viewport, so the produced texture is vertically mirrored relative to the UI;
the world-widget quad shader reads it back with a matching V so it lands
right-side-up. Colours are written in the overlay's BGRA8 space.

members.name: IsAvailable
members.doc:
True once the bridge device is up and Arc's offscreen pipelines built.
Everything no-ops (returning null textures) until it is — the screen
stack then keeps the widget on the screen-space fallback.

members.name: RenderWidget
members.signature: Ref<Image2D> RenderWidget(uint64_t owner, const Arcf::TSharedPtr<Arcf::AWidget>& widget, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, bool forceRedraw)
members.doc:
Renders `widget` into `owner`'s cached target at width x height and
returns the target's colour image for the scene renderer to sample.
Returns the existing image (no GPU work) when width/height match the
cached target and forceRedraw is false. Returns null when unavailable.

members.name: Release
members.doc: Drops the cached target for an owner that is no longer visible.

members.name: Clear
members.doc: Drops every cached target (device teardown / world change).

types.name: ArcUIComponent
types.doc:
Binds a .ui widget-tree asset to an entity. A game host that drives a
CArcUIScreenStack (SyncFromWorld each tick, overlay mounted into its Arc
root) instantiates each visible component's asset into a live Arc widget
tree, composited as a screen-space overlay ordered by ZOrder.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: ArcUIWorldWidgetComponent
types.doc:
Binds a .ui widget tree to an entity's position in the world — the
WidgetComponent analog: nameplates over players, ping markers, interaction
prompts. The host drives it through CArcUIScreenStack::SyncWorldWidgets,
which projects the entity's world position (plus offset) through the camera
and places the built tree on the overlay at that point, scaled by distance
and faded out past drawDistance. Interaction is off by default: the tree is
built hit-test invisible so it never steals gameplay clicks.

members.name: worldSpace
members.doc:
True = render the widget tree into an offscreen texture and draw it as a
real in-scene quad (depth-tested, occluded by geometry — nameplates, ping
markers). False = the legacy screen-space projection onto the 2D overlay.

members.name: faceCamera
members.doc:
World-space quad only. True = the quad always faces the camera
(billboard); false = it is oriented by the entity's transform (a plaque on
a wall). Ignored by the screen-space path.

members.name: worldWidth
members.doc:
World-space quad only. The quad's physical width in world units; its
height follows the design aspect (size.y / size.x). Drives how large the
nameplate reads in the scene independent of the design pixel size.

members.name: maxTexels
members.doc:
World-space quad only. Longest edge of the offscreen render target at the
reference distance; the LOD shrinks it further away so an idle far
nameplate costs almost nothing to re-render.

Pure keyframe math shared by the runtime player and the designer's scrub
preview: per-key easing (the curve eases INTO each key from the previous
one), clamped outside the key range, tolerant of unsorted or empty tracks.

A track with its property and every key's easing resolved, keys sorted by
time: what a playing animation evaluates each frame. The authored form
names both as strings, and evaluating it looked the easing name up for
every key it passed and compared the property name on every track, every

host-level properties (opacity/translation/scale) go through the anim host
wrapped around each target, colour goes to the named widget itself.

How PlayAnimation starts a timeline. Loop/Reverse default to the authored
flags; OnFinished fires once when a non-looping run reaches its end pose
(after the pose is applied, outside the per-screen animation loop).

types.name: FArcUIActiveAnim
types.doc:
One running timeline on a mounted screen. Owns a copy of the authored
animation so a hot-reload that evicts the asset cache can never leave the
player pointing at freed data.

Animation in its evaluated form, built on first apply (the copy above
never changes while it plays).

types.name: EArcUISlotAlign
types.doc:
How a child sits inside an auto-layout parent (box, overlay, grid) on one
axis. Default is not an alignment — it means the node never had one written,
so the parent keeps the layout it had before these fields existed.

types.name: FArcUICanvasSlot
types.doc:
A canvas slot resolved to its UMG-equivalent form: fractional anchors, the
four per-side offsets, the alignment pivot and the size-to-content flags.
Authored nodes carry the shorthand (anchor preset + position + size); this
is what both the runtime canvas and the designer lay out from, so the two
can never disagree. On an axis whose anchors coincide the high offset is
the child's size; on a stretched axis it is the inset from the far edge.

types.name: FArcUIBinding
types.doc:
One property → gameplay/Visual Script binding on a widget. Property is the widget
field driven every frame (e.g. "percent", "text"); Source is a gameplay
property path or a Visual Script expression (e.g. "Health / MaxHealth").

types.name: FArcUIExposedVar
types.doc:
One variable a widget asset exposes to whoever embeds it. The asset names
the variable, the node inside its own tree the value lands on and which
property of that node it drives; a parent that references the asset with a
UserWidget node overrides it by writing a prop under the variable's name.
Type is authoring metadata for the designer row ("text", "number", "color",
"bool", "binding"); "binding" writes a data binding instead of a literal.

types.name: FArcUIEvent
types.doc:
One widget event → host action wiring. Event names the widget delegate
("clicked", "changed", "committed"); Action is an opaque string the host's
event sink dispatches — a C++ handler name today, a Visual Script function later.
The screen stack intercepts the built-in verbs PlayAnim:/PlayAnimReverse:/
StopAnim: before the host sink sees them.

types.name: FArcUIAnimKey
types.doc:
One key on an animation track. Value carries scalar properties; Color is
read instead when the owning track animates "color". Easing names the curve
used to reach THIS key from the previous one ("linear", "cubic_out",
"back_in_out", "elastic_out", ... — the full Arc easing set in snake_case).

types.name: FArcUIAnimTrack
types.doc:
One animated property on one named widget. Property is one of "opacity",
"translation_x", "translation_y", "scale", "rotation" (applied through the
render host wrapping the target widget) or "color" (applied to the widget
itself where the type supports a live tint — Text and RichText today).
Translation is in design-space pixels, scale is a centre pivot factor,
rotation is degrees clockwise about the same centre, opacity multiplies the
whole subtree.

types.name: FArcUIAnimation
types.doc:
A named timeline on a screen: any number of tracks evaluated together.
AutoPlay starts it whenever the screen mounts (or hot-reloads in); Loop
wraps instead of finishing.

A single node in the serialized Arc widget tree: which Arc widget class to

members.name: CustomOffsetHigh

right/bottom one. Absent means the legacy symmetric behaviour (the far
inset mirrors the near one), so assets authored before it load unchanged.

members.name: CustomAnchors

members.name: CustomSlotMargin

these written must lay out byte-identically to how it did then.

types.name: FArcUIBindingLibrary
types.doc:
Resolves .ui binding sources against live gameplay state. Two source
forms are understood:
- numeric literals ("0.75") — constant values, mostly for authoring tests;
- reflection property paths ("Entity.Component.Property[.x|.y|.z|.w]") —
the entity is looked up by scene name through the injected lookup, the
component by ReflectionRegistry display/type name, the property by its
serialized or display name via the PropertyInfo tables. Vec2/3/4 and
Quat properties take an optional trailing swizzle component.
A custom hook runs before both. "visualscript.Class.Function" sources are resolved
by CArcUIScreenStack itself (shared per-class evaluation instances, per-tick
result caching) before this library is consulted.

types.name: FArcUIModalInputGate
types.doc:
"A modal screen takes the input mode to UIOnly and gives it back when it
pops" — documented behaviour that only half existed. It lived on
MGameEngine::PushUIScreen, so a screen pushed through MUIStatics (which is
how Visual Scripting and most gameplay code push one) never triggered it, and the editor
mounts its own stack and never had it at all: a modal in Play-in-editor kept
feeding gameplay while the packaged player did not.

So it is a per-tick RECONCILE against the stack's own answer rather than an
edge fired from one push site. Every path that can raise a modal goes
through the same rule, and both hosts share this one copy of it.

members.doc: Returns true when `mode` was changed and the host should apply it.

types.name: FArcUITheme
types.doc:
A game-UI theme: the named colours, fonts and metrics a .ui resolves its
tokens against. Serialized as MDF under the engine's existing .theme
extension, so it browses, cooks and validates like every other text asset.
A screen names its theme; without one the host's project theme applies, and
without that the built-in default theme — which carries exactly the colours
the factory used to hardcode, so nothing an older asset authored moves.

members.signature: bool LoadFromFile(const std::string& path, std::string* outError = nullptr)

members.name: NormalizeToken
members.doc:
"token/accent", "Content/UI/Game.theme.accent" and "AccentColor" all
name the same token: the path prefix is dropped, the rest lowercased and
run through the legacy aliases the hardcoded map understood.

members.name: HighContrastColor
members.signature: static Vec4 HighContrastColor(const std::string& normalizedToken, const Vec4& value)
members.doc:
What a colour token reads as under the player's High Contrast UI:
surfaces go black (at least 92% opaque), text goes white, and every
other colour keeps its hue at full brightness and at least half the
luminance of white, so it reads against the black surface. Tokens only —
a literal colour authored in a .ui is the author's to choose.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: FArcUIWorldWidgetMath
types.doc:
Pure geometry for the world-space UI widget quad — the part that decides
where a nameplate sits in the scene, how large its offscreen texture should
be at the current distance, whether it needs re-rendering this frame and
where a click ray lands on it in widget-local UV. Every method is static and
device-free so the headless test pins the exact transforms and hit math the
runtime uses. Matrices are row-major (worldMatrix maps a unit quad centered
on the origin, XY plane, to world space).

members.name: BillboardMatrix
members.signature: static Mat4 BillboardMatrix(const Vec3& worldPos, const Vec3& cameraPos, const Vec3& cameraUp, float widthWorld, float heightWorld)
members.doc:
Camera-facing billboard: a unit quad scaled to (widthWorld, heightWorld),
oriented so its +X follows the camera's right and +Y the camera's up,
translated to worldPos. cameraUp is the camera's world up (usually
(0,1,0)); the right axis is derived from the view direction so the quad
never rolls.

members.name: OrientedMatrix
members.signature: static Mat4 OrientedMatrix(const Mat4& entityWorld, const Vec3& localOffset, float widthWorld, float heightWorld)
members.doc:
Transform-oriented quad: the entity's world matrix supplies orientation,
`localOffset` shifts the quad along the entity's local axes, and the quad
is scaled to (widthWorld, heightWorld). A plaque bolted to a moving actor.

members.name: HeightForWidth
members.signature: static float HeightForWidth(const Vec2& designSize, float widthWorld)
members.doc:
The quad's world height from its design pixel size and physical width:
keeps the design aspect (designSize.y / designSize.x).

members.name: LodResolution
members.signature: static void LodResolution(const Vec2& designSize, float distance, float referenceDistance, uint32_t maxTexels, uint32_t& outWidth, uint32_t& outHeight)
members.doc:
Distance-driven LOD resolution for the offscreen target. At or nearer than
referenceDistance the longest edge is maxTexels; it halves per LOD as the
widget recedes, clamped to a small floor so far nameplates still render
legibly. The design aspect is preserved. Returns integer pixel extents.

members.name: LodBucket
members.signature: static uint32_t LodBucket(float distance, float referenceDistance)
members.doc:
The discrete LOD bucket a distance falls in (0 = full res at/under the
reference distance, then one step per doubling). Re-render policy keys off
this so a widget drifting slowly does not re-render every frame — only
when it crosses a bucket boundary (or its content goes dirty).

members.name: ShouldRefresh
members.signature: static bool ShouldRefresh(bool contentDirty, uint32_t lastBucket, uint32_t currentBucket)
members.doc:
Whether the offscreen texture must be re-rendered this frame: the content
changed (contentDirty), or the LOD bucket moved (resolution changed), or
nothing has been rendered yet (lastBucket == kNeverRendered).

members.name: RayQuadUV
members.signature: static bool RayQuadUV(const Vec3& rayOrigin, const Vec3& rayDir, const Mat4& worldMatrix, bool singleSided, float& outU, float& outV, float& outDistance)
members.doc:
Ray vs. the quad described by worldMatrix. On a hit, outU/outV are the
widget-local UV in [0,1] (origin top-left, matching the offscreen render
and the Arc coordinate space), outDistance the ray parameter. Returns
false when the ray misses the quad or hits its back face while
singleSided is true.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: FArcUIBindingValue
types.doc:
One resolved binding value the host supplies for a data-bound property. A
binding source resolves to a number, a string, or both; Valid is false when
the host has no value for that source (the authored default is left in place).

types.name: EArcUINavRule
types.doc:
What a gamepad/keyboard direction does from a focused widget (UE's
EUINavigation rules). Escape is the default: a spatial search across the
whole screen, keeping focus at an edge. Stop refuses to move that way even
when a neighbour exists (the last item of a menu that must not leak into the
HUD). Wrap searches spatially and, at the edge, jumps to the far end of the
same row or column. Explicit goes to a named widget regardless of layout.

types.name: FArcUINavRules
types.doc:
The four direction rules of one widget, resolved through the node tree: a
node's own nav_up / nav_down / nav_left / nav_right props override its
parent's, so a menu panel sets "wrap" once and every button inside inherits
it. Explicit targets are node names in the same screen.

members.name: ForDirection
members.signature: EArcUINavRule ForDirection(int32_t dx, int32_t dy) const

members.name: TargetForDirection
members.signature: const std::string& TargetForDirection(int32_t dx, int32_t dy) const

members.name: Resolve
members.signature: static FArcUINavRules Resolve(const FArcUINode& node, const FArcUINavRules& inherited, const std::string& namePrefix)
members.doc:
The node's own props layered over the inherited rules. `namePrefix`
qualifies explicit targets the way nested UserWidget names are.

types.name: FArcWidgetFactory
types.doc:
Turns a serialized .ui tree into a live Arc widget tree. The widget
class name on each node keys a small construction table; named nodes are
collected so a game can resolve them for script binding after instantiate.

members.name: Build
members.signature: static FBuildResult Build(const FArcUIAsset& asset, const FArcUIBindingResolver& resolver)

members.name: Build
members.signature: static FBuildResult Build(const FArcUIAsset& asset, const FBuildContext& context)

members.name: MaxUserWidgetDepth
members.doc: How deep UserWidget composition may nest before the factory refuses.

members.name: ApplyBindingValue
members.signature: static void ApplyBindingValue(const std::string& property, const FArcUIBindingValue& value, const Arcf::TSharedPtr<Arcf::AWidget>& widget)
members.doc:
Writes one resolved binding value onto a live widget. Shared between the
build-time application and the screen stack's per-frame binding pump.

members.name: SetImageDecoder
members.doc:
Process-wide image decode hook + GPU texture cache for brush images.
The cache must be cleared before the Arc bridge/device shuts down.

members.name: GetOrLoadSizedImage
members.signature: static Arcf::Ref<Arcf::IArcRHITexture> GetOrLoadSizedImage(const std::string& stem, const std::vector<int32_t>& exportedSizes, float physicalPixels)
members.doc:
One image exported at several pixel sizes ("<stem>-<N>.png"): picks the smallest
export that still covers the on-screen size, because a 512 px source sampled
down to 16 px without mips shimmers and a 16 px one stretched up blurs.

members.name: SetMediaSourceFactory
members.doc:
Process-wide clip decoder for VideoPlayer nodes, injected by the host
for the same reason the image decoder is: playback lives in Game.
Null (the default) builds every VideoPlayer as a settings-only node.

members.name: SetActiveTheme
members.doc:
Process-wide theme every build falls back to when neither the screen nor
the build context names one. Hosts point this at the project theme; the
pointer is borrowed, so the owner must outlive the last build.

members.name: ResolveColorToken
members.signature: static Arcf::ArcColor ResolveColorToken(const std::string& token, const Arcf::ArcColor& fallback)
members.doc:
Token → colour through the active theme, then the default theme. Public
because the designer resolves the same tokens for its swatches and its
token picker, and the two must never drift apart.

members.name: ComposeUserWidget
members.signature: static FArcUINode ComposeUserWidget(const FArcUINode& instance, const FArcUIAsset& referenced)
members.doc:
Composes a referenced widget asset's tree with the overrides an embedding
UserWidget node supplies: every exposed variable writes its value (or its
default) onto the target node named by the referenced asset.

members.name: ResolveRightToLeft
members.signature: static bool ResolveRightToLeft(const FArcUINode& node, bool inherited)
members.doc:
Resolves a node's flow_direction ("inherit", "ltr", "rtl") against the
parent's.

members.name: MirrorCanvasSlot
members.doc:
A canvas slot mirrored about the canvas's vertical centre line, which is
what a right-to-left canvas places its children by.

members.name: AnimHosts
members.doc:
The anim host wrapped around every node the asset's animations
target, keyed like Named. The players (screen stack, designer
preview) drive opacity/translation/scale through these.

members.name: Dependencies
members.doc:
Every other .ui this build pulled in through a UserWidget node,
so a host can rebuild the screen when one of them is saved.

members.name: Errors
members.doc:
Refused compositions (cycles, nesting past the depth cap, missing
assets). The screen still builds — the offending node becomes a
placeholder — and the host/designer reports these.

members.name: NavRules
members.doc:
Resolved navigation rules for every built widget whose rules are not
all Escape, keyed by the widget the node built (the one focus lands
on, not the drag or animation host wrapped around it).

members.name: SelfPath
members.doc:
The asset being built, used to seed cycle detection so a widget that
references itself is caught at the first hop.

members.name: Theme
members.doc:
Theme this build resolves colour tokens against. Null falls back to
the process-wide active theme, then the built-in default.

members.name: DesignerMode
members.doc:
Honour the node's designer-only flags. Off for every shipping build:
a screen must render the same whether or not somebody left a widget
hidden in the designer while authoring it.

members.name: RightToLeft
members.doc:
The flow direction a node with flow_direction "inherit" (the default)
takes at the root — the host sets it from the active culture, so one
asset serves both reading orders.

free.name: FArcUIBindingResolver
free.doc:
Host contract for data binding: given a binding source (a gameplay property
path or Visual Script expression authored in the editor), return its current value.
The screen stack passes this into Build so bound widgets pick up host state
at instantiation, then re-resolves it every Tick to keep them live.

free.name: FArcUIEventSink
free.signature: using FArcUIEventSink = std::function<void(const std::string& widgetName, const std::string& eventName, const std::string& action)>
free.doc:
Host contract for widget events: the factory wires each authored
Events { On { event, action } } entry on a node to the widget's matching
delegate; firing calls the sink with the widget's name, the event name and
the authored action string. The host decides what an action means — the
game logs/dispatches to C++ handlers today, and a visual-script-backed sink that
invokes a graph function by name attaches through the same signature later.

free.name: FArcUIImageDecoder
free.signature: using FArcUIImageDecoder = std::function<bool(const std::string& path, std::vector<uint8_t>& outRgba, uint32_t& outWidth, uint32_t& outHeight)>
free.doc:
Host contract for decoding an image asset ("Content/UI/panel.png") into
straight RGBA8 pixels. Injected by the host because image decoding lives in
a higher tier (Game/AssetSystem); the factory owns the GPU upload + cache.

free.name: FArcUIAssetProvider
free.signature: using FArcUIAssetProvider = std::function<const FArcUIAsset*(const std::string& path)>
free.doc:
Host contract for resolving a referenced widget asset ("Content/UI/Card.ui")
when a UserWidget node embeds one. The host owns the cache and the lifetime;
the returned asset must outlive the Build call. Returning null makes the node
build as a placeholder rather than failing the whole screen.

types.name: IArcUIMediaSource
types.doc:
What a VideoPlayer widget needs from a clip, and nothing about how the clip
is decoded. ArcUI sits below Game, where FMediaPlayer and the .media asset
live, so the host injects a source factory the same way it injects the
image decoder — the widget drives playback through this and samples the
frame it hands back.

members.name: Open
members.doc: A .media asset path (settings travel with it) or a bare clip path.

members.name: Update
members.doc:
Advances the clock and decodes into the frame texture. Called once per
frame by the widget's tick; nothing decodes while paused.

members.name: GetFrameTexture
members.doc:
The frame target, updated in place by Update. The source re-wraps it
whenever the underlying image is recreated, so a widget compares the
pointer it holds against this one to know when its brush went stale.

members.name: Unavailable
members.doc: No source installed: a build without online play.

members.name: Browse
members.doc: Not in a session: the server browser, Host and Direct Connect.

members.name: Lobby
members.doc: In a session, between runs: the roster, ready-up and Start.

members.name: InRun
members.doc: In a session, out on a run.

types.name: FArcLobbyModel
types.doc:
The lobby screen's logic with no widgets in it: which view to show, what the
footer may do, the status line, and the browser's ordering. The screen
rebuilds only when Poll says the state it draws from changed, so a roster
polled every frame does not tear the widget tree down sixty times a second.

members.name: CanStart
members.doc: Host, lobby phase, at least one player, everyone ready.

members.name: StatusLine
members.doc: "Waiting for 2 players to ready up", "Everyone is ready", ...

members.name: SortedServers
members.doc: The browser, joinable sessions first, then fuller ones, then by name.

members.name: ParseAddress
members.signature: static bool ParseAddress(const std::string& text, std::string& outHost, uint16_t& outPort)
members.doc:
"host", "host:port", "[v6]:port". The port defaults to 7777; a port that
is not 1-65535 or a host with spaces is refused before anything dials.

members.name: ParseAddress
members.signature: static bool ParseAddress(const std::string& text, std::string& outHost, uint16_t& outPort, std::string& outJoinKey)
members.doc: host:port#KEY — the key a direct join from another machine presents.

members.name: ExitBanner
members.doc: A banner for why the last session ended; cleared by Dismiss.

members.name: Poll
members.doc: True when anything the screen draws differs from the last Poll.

members.name: AddressDraft
members.doc: The text typed into Direct Connect survives a rebuild.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: FArcLobbyPlayer
types.doc:
One crew member as the lobby screen draws them. Plain data, not exported:
the std::string member would make MSVC demand a DLL interface for it.

members.name: Reconnecting
members.doc: The link dropped and the slot is held for the rejoin grace window.

types.name: FArcLobbyServer
types.doc: One advertised session in the server browser.

types.name: EArcLobbySessionState
types.doc: Where the local player is, which decides what the screen shows.

types.name: IArcLobbySource
types.doc:
What the lobby screen reads and drives. ArcUI sits below the networking
session in nothing it may include, so the host that owns both — the game
player — implements this over FNetSession and the platform's lobby list and
installs it (AArcUILobbyScreen::SetSourceFactory). A test drives the screen
through a fake one. Every call is safe to make in any state.

members.name: GetPhase
members.doc: 0 = lobby (the hub between runs), 1 = in a run.

members.name: GetJoinKey
members.doc:
The key a player on another machine needs to join this hosted session
directly; empty when there is none to show.

members.name: GetLastExitReason
members.doc: Why the last session ended, for the banner over the browser.

members.name: CanBrowse
members.doc:
The browser. CanBrowse is false where no platform lists sessions (no
Steam); the screen then offers only Host and Direct Connect.

members.name: JoinAddress
members.signature: virtual bool JoinAddress(const std::string& host, uint16_t port, const std::string& joinKey) = 0
members.doc:
joinKey: the host's key for a direct join from another machine,
typed after the address as host:port#KEY; empty without one.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: EArcRebindDevice
types.doc:
The two device families a rebind screen shows side by side. A row keeps one
column per family so a player can see, and change, the keyboard and the pad
binding of the same action without switching pages.

types.name: FArcRebindRow
types.doc:
One action of one context, as the screen draws it.
The data structs below carry std::string / std::vector members, so they are
deliberately NOT dllexported: exporting one makes MSVC demand a DLL
interface for every standard container inside it (C4251) while adding
nothing — they have no out-of-line members. The functions that do are
exported individually.

members.name: RuntimeOnly
members.doc:
The Enhanced-Input subsystem mirrors its mapping contexts into
runtime-only contexts rebuilt every session. Those are exactly the
actions a player wants to rebind, so the screen lists them — the
player tier is an override set precisely so it survives the rebuild.

members.name: Inactive
members.doc:
Declared but not on the context stack, so it cannot fire and cannot
collide. It still lists: a UI context waiting for its menu is a real
thing to rebind.

types.name: FArcRebindConflict
types.doc:
A pair of actions that read the same physical source. The engine never
refuses a conflicting bind — whether an overlap is intentional is a design
call — so the screen reports it and lets the player decide.

types.name: FArcRebindModel
types.doc:
Backs the in-game rebinding screen: enumerates every action the action
system currently carries, captures a new source while in the listening
state, reports conflicts, and writes through the player tier
(<project>/Saved/Config/InputUser.mdfb).

members.name: RowsIn
members.signature: std::vector<const FArcRebindRow*> RowsIn(const std::string& contextName) const

members.name: IsCapturing
members.doc:
While capturing, the host must route raw input here instead of at the
game: the whole point is to read the key the player pressed, including
keys that are already bound to something.

members.name: BeginCapture
members.signature: bool BeginCapture(const std::string& contextName, const std::string& actionName, EArcRebindDevice device)

members.name: CaptureKey
members.doc: Each returns true when the capture was accepted and the binding written.

members.name: ResetAction
members.signature: void ResetAction(const std::string& contextName, const std::string& actionName)

members.name: Save
members.doc: Writes the override set to the player tier.

members.name: DescribeBinding
members.doc:
"W", "Left Mouse", "Gamepad South", "Gamepad LeftX" — what a key cap
shows. Empty for a binding shape that has no player-facing name.

types.name: EArcSettingCategory
types.doc:
The six screens a player expects to find in a pause menu. Anything the
editor exposes that is not one of these is a developer knob and stays in
Project Settings.

types.name: EArcSettingBackend
types.doc:
Where the value actually lives. Cvar rows go through IConsoleManager the
way the editor's pages do; GlobalConfig rows are the handful of knobs the
engine reads out of the config directly (the audio bus volumes); Host rows
are the ones no lower tier can reach — window mode, resolution, monitor and
refresh rate all live behind EngineLoop's DisplaySettings, which sits above
this module, so the runtime host installs the applier instead.

types.name: FArcSettingChoice
types.doc:
The data structs below carry std::string / std::vector members, so they are
deliberately NOT dllexported: exporting one makes MSVC demand a DLL
interface for every standard container inside it (C4251) while adding
nothing — they have no out-of-line members. The functions that do are
exported individually.

types.name: FArcSettingRow
types.doc:
One row of the settings screen. Labels, defaults and descriptions are
copied from the editor's Project Settings pages rather than reinvented, so
the two screens never disagree about what a knob does.

members.name: CompanionKey
members.doc:
A second key written alongside the first from the same choice index —
the GI method row drives r.DDGI and r.SSGI together, exactly as the
editor's rendering page does.

members.name: Enabled
members.doc:
A row the device, the graphics API or this game rules out is removed from
the model (BuildModel logs why at debug level), so every row a screen
receives is one the player can change; a host may still clear this to
show a control read-only.

members.name: NeedsConfirmation
members.doc:
Changing this can leave the player looking at a black screen, so Apply
arms the confirmation countdown instead of committing outright.

members.name: NeedsRestart
members.doc:
The value only reaches the running game on the next launch. The editor
says so in its own hints; the player screen has to as well.

types.name: FArcDeviceProfile
types.doc:
What the device and the active graphics API can do, flattened away from RHI
so the model is constructible with no device at all. Probe fills it from the
live backend; a test fills it by hand.

members.name: ApiRayTracing
members.doc:
The static API ceiling — false means no driver will ever answer, so the
control is greyed naming the API rather than the GPU.

members.name: ApiFSR
members.doc:
Per-technology API ceilings (FRHIApiCeiling::SupportsUpscaler /
SupportsFrameGenBackend / SupportsReflex): an option the API can never
host is not offered at all.

members.name: DynamicFrameGeneration
members.doc: DLSS-G dynamic Multi Frame Generation, as the driver reports it.

members.name: MaxFrameGenMultiplier
members.doc:
Largest presented-per-rendered multiplier the frame-generation backend
reports for this GPU (FrameGeneration::GetMaxMultiplier).

members.name: DLSS
members.doc:
Live, per device: IUpscaler::IsUpscalerSupported for the upscalers,
FrameGeneration::IsBackendSupported for the interpolators and
Reflex::IsSupported — never the compile-time SDK gates.

members.name: VendorRuntimesProbed
members.doc:
False when the live per-device fields above were not asked for and only
repeat the API ceiling: answering them loads and initialises Streamline,
NGX, XeSS and XeLL, about 2 s of a start that uses none of them.

types.name: FArcDisplayOption
types.doc:
One entry of a Display choice list. The host fills these — EngineLoop's
DisplaySettings owns monitor and mode enumeration and sits above this
module.

types.name: FGameUserSettings
types.doc:
UE5's GameUserSettings, in the shape this engine already has: cvars for the
renderer knobs, GlobalConfig for the audio buses, and a per-user MDF file
under <project>/Saved/Config that keeps the player's choices out of the
committed project tier.

members.name: FHostApplier
members.signature: using FHostApplier = std::function<void(const FArcSettingRow& row, const std::string& value, bool persist)>
members.doc:
`persist` is false for the startup push, which is replaying values the
store already holds — or, on a fresh machine, the table defaults. A host
that writes its own file must honour it, or first launch overwrites a
configuration some other path wrote and stamps it as the player's.

members.name: StorePath
members.doc:
<project>/Saved/Config/GameUserSettings.ini, or the per-user product dir
when no project is open. Never the project's Config dir: that one is
committed and belongs to the team, not to one player's machine.

members.name: BuildModel
members.doc:
Builds every row against the given device profile. Safe to call again —
pending edits are dropped and the applied values re-read.

members.name: EnsureVendorRuntimesProbed
members.doc:
A model built without the vendor runtimes offers every choice the API
allows. The settings screen calls this before it shows anything: the
model is rebuilt from a full probe and the store read again, so a
choice this GPU cannot run is withdrawn. True when it rebuilt.

members.name: FindRow
members.signature: const FArcSettingRow* FindRow(const std::string& key) const

members.name: AmbiguousChoiceRows
members.doc:
One entry per pair of choices in one row that carry the same value. The
combo box, the companion write and the saved file all resolve a choice BY
value, so such a pair is unrepresentable: the player picks one option and
a different one is applied. Must come back empty; BuildModel logs any
entry as an error.

members.name: SetPending
members.signature: bool SetPending(const std::string& key, const std::string& value)
members.doc:
Stages an edit. Refused for a row the device cannot do, which is what
keeps a greyed control from being driven by a stale saved file.

members.name: Apply
members.doc:
Pushes every staged value at its backend and writes the store. Returns
false only when the store could not be written — the values are live
either way, because refusing what the player just asked for is worse
than a settings file that failed to save.

members.name: Revert
members.doc: Throws the staged edits away.

members.name: IsAwaitingConfirmation
members.doc:
A mode change that leaves the display dark cannot be undone by a player
who cannot see the screen, so Apply arms a countdown and reverts on its
own unless the player confirms.

members.name: TickConfirmation
members.doc:
Drive from the UI tick. True on the frame the countdown ran out and the
previous display values were put back.

members.name: ApplyToBackends
members.doc:
Pushes the applied values at their backends without touching the file —
the startup path, run once the model is built and the store is read.

members.name: SetHostApplier
members.doc:
The runtime host owns the window, so it owns everything the Display
category actually changes. Without an applier those rows still record
and persist; they simply do not take effect.

members.name: SetAppliesArcPalette
members.doc:
Whether High Contrast UI also swaps Arc's Mowo palette (the colours the
settings screen and other built-in menus paint with). Only the game
host turns it on: the editor owns that palette through its Appearance
preference, and a game setting must never repaint the editor.

members.name: ApplyArcPalette
members.doc:
Loads a Mowo palette file (the editor's theme JSON: a "colors" table of
token name → "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA") over the default colours, or
resets to the defaults when the path is empty. Returns the number of
colours applied.

members.name: RefreshDisplayOptions
members.doc:
Refills the choice lists of the Host rows from the provider. Called by
BuildModel, and again by the screen when a monitor is hot-plugged.

types.name: MRebindStatics
types.doc:
The input-remapping surface for a game that builds its own controls
screen in Visual Scripting or ArcUI instead of using the stock rebind screen: list
every action with its keyboard and gamepad binding, start listening for a
new one, feed it the first key, button or stick the player touches
(PollRebindCapture each frame while listening), show conflicts, reset and
save to the player's own tier. One model shared by every caller, the same
FArcRebindModel the stock screen drives. Device: 0 keyboard/mouse, 1 pad.

members.signature: std::string GetRebindLabel(int32_t index, int32_t device) const

members.name: IsRebindConflicting
members.signature: bool IsRebindConflicting(int32_t index, int32_t device) const

members.name: PollRebindCapture
members.doc: True on the frame a capture lands (and the binding is written).

members.name: SetWidgetText
members.signature: void SetWidgetText(const std::string& screen, const std::string& widget, const std::string& text)

members.name: SetWidgetVisible
members.signature: void SetWidgetVisible(const std::string& screen, const std::string& widget, bool visible)

types.name: AArcUIAnimHost
types.doc:
Transparent single-child wrapper the widget factory inserts around every
node an animation targets. Layout-transparent always: it reports the child's
desired size and hands the child a rect of its full allotted size. Animation
state only moves how that rect is drawn — translation shifts it (design
pixels, scaled to the viewport by the screen-root canvas), scale and
rotation are a render transform about its centre (painted, and inverted for
hit testing), opacity multiplies the whole subtree through the renderer's
layer stack. No setter invalidates layout: a pulsing button never
re-measures or re-wraps its text.

members.name: OnPaint
members.signature: int32_t OnPaint(const CArcPaintArgs& args, const CGeometry& geo, CArcUIRenderer& renderer, int32_t layerId) const override

members.name: BuildRotationMatrix
members.doc:
Rotation about the child's centre, in absolute pixels. Identity while the
rotation track is at zero, which is what keeps the untouched UI on the
renderer's no-transform fast path.

members.name: BuildRenderTransform
members.doc: Scale then rotation about the child's centre; identity at rest.

members.name: SetDesignUnitScale
members.doc:
The design-pixel → viewport-pixel factor translations are multiplied by.
The screen-root canvas writes it at the top of every arrange pass, so
hosts below it read the value of the screen they belong to.

types.name: AArcUICanvas
types.doc:
A UMG-style canvas: children are placed by anchor + offset + explicit size
within this widget's allotted rect. Arc ships a CCanvasSlot struct but no
panel that consumes it, so the ArcUI runtime carries its own — the one
widget the .ui factory needs that the framework does not provide.

members.name: SetScreenRoot
members.doc:
Only the canvas a screen's root node builds insets by the safe zone;
nested canvases sit inside an already-inset rect.

members.name: OnPaint
members.signature: int32_t OnPaint(const CArcPaintArgs& args, const CGeometry& geo, CArcUIRenderer& renderer, int32_t layerId) const override

members.name: GetNumChildren
members.doc:
Children are enumerated front-to-back in ZOrder, so Arc's reverse-order
hit test picks the same widget the painter drew on top.

members.name: GetChildAtSlot
members.doc:
Insertion order — the order the authored node children were added, which
is what the designer maps its node paths onto.

members.name: CanSkipArrange
members.doc:
The arrange body is anchors, slot offsets and the children's cached
desired sizes against the allotted rect — no clock, no clamped offset,
no row recycling — and the one input it reads from outside the tree (the
safe-zone inset) invalidates every widget when it moves. Paint is the
children in ZOrder at the geometry arrange gave them.

Without these the root of every .ui screen refused, and one refusing
descendant vetoes every ancestor, so a shipped game re-arranged and
repainted its whole UI tree every frame.

members.name: ComputeChildRect
members.signature: static ArcRect ComputeChildRect(const ::Mowo::FArcUICanvasSlot& slot, const ArcVec2& parentSize, const ArcVec2& desiredSize, float scale)
members.doc:
The one place canvas geometry is computed. Anchors are fractions of the
parent rect; on an axis whose anchors coincide the slot's high offset is
the child's size and Alignment is its pivot, otherwise the high offset is
the inset from the far edge. Offsets and sizes are authored in design
units and multiplied by scale; anchors track the real viewport.

members.name: ComputeDpiScale
members.signature: static float ComputeDpiScale(const ArcVec2& viewport, const ArcVec2& design)
members.doc:
Uniform design→viewport scale (aspect-preserving fit) so a canvas authored
at its design resolution lays out proportionally at any viewport size.

members.name: SetSafeZoneInsets
members.doc:
Title-safe insets as a fraction of each axis, applied by screen-root
canvases. A project setting on the host side; 0 disables.

types.name: AArcUILobbyScreen
types.doc:
The co-op front door: a server browser with Host and Direct Connect while
the player is in no session, the crew's ready-up lobby between runs, and a
call-back card while the crew is out. It reads and drives an
IArcLobbySource — the game player installs one over FNetSession and the
platform's lobby list — so the same screen runs in a test against a fake.

The tree is rebuilt only when FArcLobbyModel::Poll reports a change, from
the stack's per-frame TickAll, so a roster update or a server list landing
shows up without the game wiring a refresh.

types.name: AArcUIRebindScreen
types.doc:
The in-game control-rebinding screen: one tab per input context, one row per
action, a key cap per device family. Clicking a cap puts it into the
listening state; the host then feeds the next raw key, button or axis to
the model.

The model writes through the player tier
(<project>/Saved/Config/InputUser.mdfb), never the project's committed
Config dir, so a rebind belongs to the player and survives the
Enhanced-Input contexts being rebuilt from asset data each session.

types.name: AArcUISettingsScreen
types.doc:
The player-facing settings screen: a category rail on the left, the rows of
the selected category on the right, and Apply / Revert / Reset along the
bottom. It reads FGameUserSettings, which reads the same cvars the editor's
Project Settings pages write, so the two never drift apart.

A row the device cannot drive is drawn greyed with the reason beside it
rather than hidden — a control that vanishes tells a player nothing about
why their machine will not do the thing the box promised.

widget tick, so the screen stack advances every live screen through

a player who could not see the new resolution had no way back.

members.name: AArcUIStatOverlay
members.doc:
Purely decorative, and it stretches over the whole window: left
hit-testable it sits on top of the entire UI and swallows every pointer
event, which looks exactly like an editor that has stopped responding to
the mouse while it still draws and still takes the keyboard. The
guarantee belongs here rather than at each call site, because the whole
point of this widget is that a host parks one in its tree forever.

chrome leaves it at zero.

types.name: AArcUIWorldLayer
types.doc:
Hosts world-anchored widget trees on the screen-space overlay: each child is
placed at the projected screen position of the entity it belongs to, scaled
by distance and faded out past its draw distance. This is the projection
half of a UMG WidgetComponent — the tree is real Arc UI, its placement comes
from the camera rather than from a canvas slot. Painted back to front so a
nameplate nearer the camera covers one behind it.

types.name: AVideoPlayer
types.doc:
UMG's MediaPlayer + Image pairing in one node: binds a .media asset, owns
the playback controls Visual Script reaches through MUIStatics, and shows the
decoded frame through a hosted AImage so the picture takes the same
brush path every other image on the screen does. The decode itself lives
behind IArcUIMediaSource; without a source factory installed the widget
builds, holds its settings and paints its backdrop, so a headless build
of the screen still reports the node.

members.name: SetSource
members.doc:
Opens the asset through the installed source factory; an empty path
closes whatever is open. AutoPlay starts the clip on success.

members.name: AdoptSource
members.doc:
Hands the widget a source directly — the host-side seam and the test
seam, so a fake clip can stand in for the decoder.

members.name: SetKeepAspect
members.doc: Letterbox the frame inside the node instead of stretching it.

members.name: Tick
members.doc:
Advances the clip and refreshes the hosted image when the frame target
was recreated. The screen stack drives this through TickAll.
